summary: Phase 2b LiveKit Calls — full backend coverage (14/14 pass) + frontend verification via Playwright. Backend: /api/calls/config, /api/calls/start (audio + video + rejoined), /api/calls/{id}/join (with 404/400 guards), /api/calls/{id}/end (initiator-vs-non-initiator branching), /api/calls/by-chat/{chat_id}, /api/calls/{id}, /api/webhooks/livekit (401 on bad/no auth) all behave per spec. JWT tokens validated as 3-part base64url, >200 chars. System messages (call_started + call_ended) posted with correct metadata. Frontend: AI chat correctly hides audio/video buttons; non-AI chats show both [data-testid=start-audio-call-btn] and [data-testid=start-video-call-btn]; clicking opens /call/new?chat=...&mode=audio|video in a new tab; MessageBubble CallRecordCard correctly renders green LIVE pulse + JOIN CALL for call_started and gray ENDED + duration for call_ended (verified visually in chat screenshot, multiple LIVE + ENDED cards present). Regression: iteration11_phase2a (33) + iteration10_referrals (27) all pass = 60/60.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 2645 lines — Phase 2b added ~240 lines for calls. Splitting into routers (calls_router.py, voice_router.py, admin_router.py, approvals_router.py) is strongly recommended before Phase 2c lands more endpoints.

call_service.receive_webhook swallows any exception inside end_room (call_service.py:58) — fine for resilience but the bare 'except Exception: pass' will hide real LiveKit Cloud auth/network failures. Consider logging at warning level.

In server.py end_call (line 2545), the condition `len(still_active) == 0 or is_initiator` correctly ends the call when initiator leaves; but if the initiator joins, leaves, and someone else is still active, the call is force-ended. Spec wording 'non-initiator only marks left_at; call remains active if others still in' is fully met by current code. However the inverse (initiator can also leave-without-ending via UI) is not exposed — every initiator hangup ends the whole call. Confirm this is the intended UX.

started_at parsing on line 2547 uses 'T' in call['started_at'] to decide between fromisoformat and now() — this is brittle. now_iso() always returns ISO with 'T', so the else branch is dead code; safe but misleading. Just use datetime.fromisoformat directly.

CallRoom.jsx handleDisconnected navigates to /chats/{chat_id} on disconnect — if conn is null at the moment LiveKitRoom errors out (e.g. getUserMedia denied), it navigates to '/chats/' which redirects to '/'. Consider falling back to /chats when chat_id missing.
CallRoom.jsx CallShell: useEffect for elapsed timer (line 145) does not clear setInterval if call.started_at is invalid. Low priority but worth a guard.
